game-state.description: The host's authoritative ground-truth state for one active game, as persisted to game.json and exposed only via host-token-gated endpoints. Per-player turn files are derived from this (fog-of-war filtered) and have their own schema; this is never sent to a non-host client. See docs/architecture.rst.

id.description: UUID v4 — the engine's canonical identifier for this game.

planet_states.description: Mutable per-planet ground truth, keyed by planet id (stringified u32).

player_messages.description: Host-only per-turn message accumulator, keyed by player id (stringified u32). Each turn-resolution step appends to the owning player's list (see resolve_turn in engine/src/game/turn/mod.rs); the list is cleared at the start of every resolution so messages are strictly per-turn, never accumulated across years. player_view() merges this with the view-time messages it derives (e.g. the empty-production-queue nudge) to build the player's turn file. Absent on pre-existing saves predating the message store; treated as empty. See docs/mechanics/turn_resolution.rst.

fleets.description: All fleets in the game, keyed by fleet id (stringified u32) — host-side ground truth. Fleet ids share the universe-wide space-object id space with planet ids: a planet id and a fleet id are never equal within a game, so a message's related-object and a client 'Goto' address either kind by the one id (see docs/architecture.rst). Per-player turn files expose only the fleets a player may see (own in full; others within scanner coverage), derived in game/view.rs; raw state is never sent to a non-host client. Absent on pre-existing saves predating the fleet model; treated as empty.

fleet.description: A named group of ships at a location, with an ordered waypoint list — host-side ground truth. A fleet holds only ship designs (kind=ship); starbases live on planets, not in fleets. See docs/gameplay/fleets.rst and docs/mechanics/fleet_movement.rst.

id.description: Universe-wide space-object id, unique across every planet and fleet in this game.

x.description: Current X coordinate (light years). Equals the orbited planet's X when orbiting_planet_id is set.

orbiting_planet_id.description: Planet id this fleet orbits, or null when in deep space. When set, (x, y) equals that planet's position.

ship_stacks.description: Ship composition: one entry per ship design the fleet contains, with how many ships of that design.

fuel.description: Fuel on board (mg), shared across the whole fleet. Bounded in play by the summed tank capacity of the fleet's designs; the stored value is ground truth.

waypoints.description: Ordered list of future destinations, each with a travel warp and an order to run on arrival. Empty for an idle fleet with no pending orders. The fleet's current position is (x, y), not a waypoint.

repeat_orders.description: When true the waypoint chain cycles back to the first waypoint after the last waypoint's order runs (automated freighter loops). See docs/mechanics/fleet_movement.rst 'Repeat Orders'.

ship-stack.description: A group of identical ships in a fleet: `count` ships built from the owner's ship design in slot `design_slot`.

design_slot.description: The owner's ship-design slot (0–15) these ships are built from.

count.description: Number of ships of this design in the fleet (≥1; an emptied stack is removed).

fleet-cargo.description: Minerals and colonists carried by a fleet, in kT. Bounded in play by the fleet's cargo capacity; the stored value is ground truth.

colonists.description: Colonists aboard, in kT (the original tracks colonists in units of 100; cargo here is kT).

fleet-waypoint.description: One destination in a fleet's route: where to go, how fast, and what to do on arrival. See docs/mechanics/fleet_movement.rst 'Waypoints'.

target_planet_id.description: Planet id this waypoint targets, when the destination is a planet (its position equals x, y). Null for a bare-coordinate waypoint.

warp.description: Warp speed to travel to this waypoint (0–10; 10 is the ramscoop free 'safe speed'). Distance covered is warp² ly per year.

fleet-waypoint-task.description: Order a fleet runs on reaching a waypoint. See docs/mechanics/fleet_movement.rst 'Waypoint orders'.

player-message.description: One host-side turn-resolution message queued for a player, before projection into that player's turn file. Mirrors the turn-file turn-message shape (schemas/response-turn-file.json) WITHOUT the id — player_view() assigns a contiguous 0-based id at projection time, since ids are only meaningful within the turn file a message is projected into.

message.description: The rendered display text. The turn-file wire type (schemas/response-turn-file.json) documents the original client's 1024-char cap; the engine keeps messages well under it, so this host-side store leaves the length unconstrained.

message-type.description: Stable tag for the kind of message (the turn-message-type family in schemas/turn.json), e.g. 'PlanetProductionQueueEmpty'. A client treats it as an opaque tag and never derives importance from it.

related-object.description: Universe-wide space-object id (a planet or fleet) this message is about — the client's 'Goto' subject. Absent for a message with no on-map subject.

related-battle.description: Id of the battle this message reports on, when it is a combat message. Absent otherwise.

important.description: Whether this message survives the player's 'hide unimportant messages' filter. The engine classifies importance when the message is produced; a client never derives it from message-type.

universe.description: Static, shared map data (the .xy-equivalent): identity and position only. Mutable planet state lives in game-state.planet_states, not here.

width.description: Side length of the square boundary in light years.

planets.description: All planets, keyed by planet id (stringified u32).

planet-static.description: Static planet data (the .xy-equivalent): identity and position, constant for the lifetime of the game.

x.description: X coordinate within the universe boundary (light years).

planet-state.description: Mutable per-game planet state — host-side ground truth. Hab values are in original-game units: gravity is one of 101 discrete floats (0.12–8.00), temperature an integer -200..+200 step 4, radiation an integer 0..100.

owner.description: Owning player id, or null if unowned.

defenses.description: Planetary defense installations built here (0..100), buildable id 9. Built via production (defenses production is a later slice), so 0 until then. The best-researched defense TYPE and the resulting coverage are derived per-view from the owner's tech, not stored. Absent on pre-existing saves predating the defense model; treated as 0.

build_queue.description: Ordered production queue for this planet. Items are built top-to-bottom at turn resolution (see docs/mechanics/production.rst). Absent on pre-existing saves predating the queue; treated as empty.

route_target.description: Planet id that arriving route-flagged fleets are forwarded to, or null for no route (the planet's "Route To" destination). Absent on pre-existing saves predating routing; treated as null.

starbase_design_slot.description: The owning player's starbase-design slot (0–9) whose design is built in orbit here, or null for no starbase. A planet has at most one starbase (docs/mechanics/starbase_design.rst). Host-only ground truth; its derived stats are projected into the turn file separately. Absent on pre-existing saves predating the starbase model; treated as null.

packet_target.description: Planet id this planet's mass driver launches mineral packets toward, or null for no target (set via the planet.set_packet_target order; requires a mass driver on the planet's starbase). Packet flight/decay/arrival are resolved separately. Absent on pre-existing saves predating packet targeting; treated as null.

build-item.description: One entry in a planet's production queue. build_object_id indexes the buildable registry (GET /model/buildables); build_progress is server-managed (0 for a freshly queued item).

build_object_id.description: Buildable registry id (e.g. 7=factory, 8=mine, 9=defenses; 1024+N=design slot N). See docs/mechanics/production.rst.

build_quantity.description: Number of this item remaining to build.

build_progress.description: Percent complete (0..99) of the item currently at the head of this entry.

tech-levels.description: A player's current technology level in each of the six fields.

player.description: A player (human or NPC): links a race to in-game state. NPC players share this shape.

homeworld_id.description: Planet id of this player's homeworld, or null before placement.

race.description: Full race definition. Optional: pre-existing games may have been persisted without it; new games always set it, and per-player view derivation requires it.

designs.description: The player's stored ship and starbase designs. Optional/defaulted for back-compat with games persisted before the design model; new games set []. Edited via design.upsert / design.delete orders; projected into the owner's turn file as ship-designs.

slot-assignment.description: One filled hull slot in a stored design: which component sits in which slot, and how many.

slot-index.description: Index into the hull's slots array.

part-id.description: Component installed; indexes the technology catalog.

count.description: How many of the part occupy this slot.

ship-design.description: A stored ship or starbase design owned by a player. built-count is NOT stored here: it is derived from the player's live fleets when a turn file is projected. See docs/mechanics/ship_design.rst.

slot.description: Design slot index (ships 0-15, starbases 0-9 in a parallel space disambiguated by kind).

kind.description: Whether this is a ship or starbase design.

hull-id.description: Hull id (ship-hull when kind=ship, starbase-hull when kind=starbase).
